links.outcome: LLM insulin dosing failure modes including arithmetic errors in simulator
links.effect: LLMs showed arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, inconsistent clinical logic, and overly aggressive insulin dosing with chain-of-thought prompting.
links.quote: However, LLMs exhibit notable limitations, such as overly aggressive insulin dosing when prompted with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, highlighting critical failure modes including arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, and inconsistent clinical logic.

links.outcome: Zero-shot LLM insulin dosing performance versus trained RL agents in simulator
links.effect: Carefully prompted smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) achieved comparable or superior clinical performance versus trained SRAs, particularly in stable cohorts; limitations in other settings.
links.quote: Our results indicate that carefully designed zero-shot prompts enable smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) to achieve comparable or superior clinical performance relative to extensively trained SRAs, particularly in stable patient cohorts.
